anvil:aws:DSQL.description: Serverless distributed PostgreSQL-compatible database. Secure-by-default Aurora DSQL cluster with optional multi-region active-active replication, IAM authentication, deploy-time role bootstrapping, and AWS Backup integration. No VPC required — connect directly via IAM auth tokens.

backup.description: AWS Backup configuration. Omit to disable. When set, Anvil opts in the DSQL resource type per region, creates a backup plan with retention and schedule, and for multi-region clusters automatically adds cross-region copy rules.

multiRegion.description: Opt-in multi-region configuration. When set, Anvil creates two clusters in the specified regions and links them via ClusterPeering. When omitted, a single-region cluster is created in the provider's default region.

schemas.description: Schemas and the tables within them. Anvil creates each schema and table (additive-only — new tables/columns/indexes are applied; removals are left to humans). Omit to skip table management.

stream.description: Sends the cluster's change data capture (CDC) events, every committed row change in every table, to a Kinesis Data Stream. Anvil creates the IAM role DSQL writes with; `anvil deploy` creates the CDC stream after the rest of the stack, and `anvil destroy` deletes it first. Removing it deletes the CDC stream, and changes made while it's gone are never captured. Omit to keep CDC off.

vpc.description: Optional VPC configuration. When set without hasNat, Anvil creates interface VPC endpoints (PrivateLink) per region so traffic stays on the AWS backbone. When omitted, the Lambda connects to the public DSQL endpoint over the internet using IAM auth tokens over TLS.

clusterArns.description: Map of region to cluster ARN. Single-region: one entry. Multi-region: one entry per region. e.g. { "us-east-1": "arn:aws:dsql:us-east-1:..." }.

endpoint.description: The single cluster endpoint for the provider's default region. Convenience for the common single-region case — pass straight to a Lambda env var: { DSQL_ENDPOINT: dsql.endpoint }. For multi-region this is the local-region endpoint; use endpoints[region] for another.

endpoints.description: Map of region to cluster endpoint. Single-region: one entry keyed by the provider region. Multi-region: one entry per region. e.g. { "us-east-1": "abc123.dsql.us-east-1.on.aws" }. Pass the relevant endpoint to your Lambda via environment variables.

rolesTableName.description: DynamoDB table name for role bootstrap. Passed to DSQLConnect (via grantConnect) so it can create the IAM role-mapping item. Empty when no roles are configured.

streamKinesisArn.description: The Kinesis stream CDC events are sent to. Empty when stream is omitted.

streamRoleArn.description: The IAM role DSQL writes CDC events with: the one Anvil created, or stream.roleArn. Empty when stream is omitted.

vpcEndpointIds.description: Map of region to VPC endpoint ID. Only populated when vpc is set and hasNat is false. Pass to LambdaVpcEndpointArgs.endpointId.

vpcEndpointSecurityGroupIds.description: Map of region to VPC endpoint security group ID. Only populated when vpc is set and hasNat is false. Pass to LambdaVpcEndpointArgs.securityGroupId: the SG allows its members to reach the endpoint on port 5432, so joining it is what gives the Lambda network access.

anvil:aws:DSQLBackupArgs.description: AWS Backup configuration for DSQL clusters. Anvil opts in the DSQL resource type in each cluster region, creates a backup plan, and for multi-region clusters automatically adds cross-region copy rules so restores work in both regions.

retentionDays.description: Number of days to retain recovery points. Default: 35.

scheduleExpression.description: CRON expression for when backups run. e.g. "cron(0 2 * * ? *)". Default: daily at midnight — cron(0 0 * * ? *).

scheduleTimezone.description: IANA timezone for the schedule expression. e.g. "Australia/Sydney". Default: "Etc/UTC". Anvil passes this to the backup plan rule as scheduleExpressionTimezone.

vaultArn.description: ARN of an existing backup vault to store recovery points in. When omitted, Anvil uses the default AWS Backup vault.

anvil:aws:DSQLColumn.description: A single column in a table.

default.description: Raw SQL default expression, passed through verbatim. String literals need inner quotes: "'active'". Functions: "now()".

notNull.description: Adds NOT NULL. Primary-key columns are auto-NOT-NULL.

unique.description: Creates a named async unique index on this column.

anvil:aws:DSQLColumnType.description: A DSQL-supported column type. Arrays, enums, serial, money, and xml are intentionally excluded — DSQL does not support them.

enum.description: Universally unique identifier (recommended for primary keys).
Date and time without time zone.
Date and time with time zone.
Create a foreign key reference to the table.

anvil:aws:DSQLIndex.description: A secondary index on a table. Created with CREATE INDEX ASYNC (DSQL requirement); the build runs in the background.

name.description: Index name (required, used for additive diffing).

anvil:aws:DSQLMultiRegionArgs.description: Multi-region configuration for DSQL. When set, Anvil creates one cluster per region and links them via ClusterPeering. Both regions are active-active — reads and writes are accepted at either endpoint with strong consistency.

regions.description: The two AWS regions to deploy the cluster into. Anvil creates one cluster per region using internally-created regional providers. AWS validates the region and witness region combination — Anvil passes through without inference.

witnessRegion.description: The AWS region to use as the witness. Stores a limited window of encrypted transaction logs to improve multi-region durability. Must be a third region distinct from both cluster regions. AWS validates this — Anvil does not infer or default it.

anvil:aws:DSQLOverrides.description: Low-level overrides for the underlying aws.dsql.Cluster resource. Use for KMS key ARN and any other cluster-level settings not exposed by the Anvil API.

kmsEncryptionKey.description: ARN of a KMS CMK for encryption at rest. If omitted, AWS_OWNED_KMS_KEY is used (default — always on, zero cost).

tags.description: Additional tags to apply to the cluster resources.

anvil:aws:DSQLRole.description: A database role within a schema (its parent). Role names must be globally unique across all schemas — DSQL roles are database-wide. grants apply to the parent schema; tableScoping optionally narrows to specific tables.

grants.description: Table-level privileges to grant to this role on all current and future tables in the schema. e.g. ["SELECT", "INSERT", "UPDATE", "DELETE"]. Applied via GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES.

name.description: The Postgres role name. e.g. "app_role". Must be a valid PostgreSQL identifier.

tableScoping.description: Optionally narrow the grants to specific tables instead of the whole schema. When set, the role is granted only on these tables (which must exist — declare them in schemas[]). When omitted, grants apply schema-wide (current + future tables).

anvil:aws:DSQLSchema.description: A schema and the tables within it. Anvil creates the schema (CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS) and each table.

roles.description: Database roles for this schema. Each role's grants apply to this schema. Role names must be globally unique across all schemas.

tables.description: Tables to create in this schema.

anvil:aws:DSQLStreamArgs.description: Change data capture to a Kinesis Data Stream.

kinesisArn.description: The Kinesis Data Stream that receives the events, e.g. a KinesisStream's arn. Must be in the cluster's region (the provider region for multi-region clusters) and accept records of at least 2048 KiB, which is KinesisStream's default.

kmsKeyArn.description: The customer-managed KMS key the Kinesis stream is encrypted with, if any. Anvil's role is then also allowed kms:GenerateDataKey on it. Not needed with the AWS-managed key (KinesisStream's default). Only valid without roleArn.

roleArn.description: An existing IAM role for DSQL to write with. Omit to have Anvil create one that only this cluster can assume, allowed to write to kinesisArn only.

anvil:aws:DSQLTable.description: A table to create in a schema. Additive-only: Anvil creates the table and adds new columns/indexes, but never drops or alters existing ones.

primaryKey.description: Column names forming the primary key, in order. Required — DSQL uses the PK as the distribution key and it cannot be added after creation. AWS recommends a uuid PK generated app-side.

anvil:aws:DSQLVpcArgs.description: VPC configuration for DSQL. When set without hasNat, Anvil creates interface VPC endpoints per region so traffic stays on the AWS backbone. When hasNat is true, endpoint creation is skipped and traffic routes via the existing NAT gateway to the public DSQL endpoint. Anvil never creates the NAT gateway.

hasNat.description: Signal that a NAT gateway already exists in this VPC. When true, Anvil skips interface endpoint creation — the Lambda routes to the public DSQL endpoint via NAT. When false (default), Anvil creates interface endpoints per region.

privateSubnetIds.description: The IDs of the private subnets to attach the endpoint ENIs to. One ENI is created per subnet. Pass all private subnet IDs — typically one per AZ. Accepts Output<string[]> — pass vpc.privateSubnetIds directly.

vpcId.description: The ID of the VPC. Accepts Output<string> — pass vpc.vpcId directly.

deletionProtectionEnabled.description: Whether deletion protection is enabled in this cluster. Default value is `false`.

forceDestroy.description: Destroys cluster even if `deletionProtectionEnabled` is set to `true`. Default value is `false`.

kmsEncryptionKey.description: The ARN of the AWS KMS key that encrypts data in the DSQL Cluster, or `"AWS_OWNED_KMS_KEY"`.

multiRegionProperties.description: Multi-region properties of the DSQL Cluster.

region.description: Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints). Defaults to the Region set in the provider configuration.

tags.description: Set of tags to be associated with the AWS DSQL Cluster resource.
